examples.title: Half adder
examples.description: An XOR gate for the sum and an AND gate for the carry. Flip A and B through all four combinations, then open the truth table.

examples.title: Full adder
examples.description: Two half-adder blocks and an OR gate. The first example that uses blocks: it is the circuit inside every stage of the 4-bit adder.

examples.title: 4-bit adder
examples.description: Four full-adder blocks in a ripple chain, two levels of nesting. Flip A0–A3 and B0–B3 to add two 4-bit numbers.

examples.title: 3-bit counter
examples.description: A clock and three D flip-flops. Press Run (F5) and watch the bits count in the timing diagram.

examples.title: SR latch
examples.description: Two cross-coupled NOR gates: memory without a clock. Set, then reset, and see that it holds in between.

examples.title: Ring oscillator
examples.description: Three inverters in a ring. The loop can never settle, so LogicBench outlines it and reports it instead of hanging.
